safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes lip swelling but does not document the duration as “past 1 hour” (no clear elapsed time stated).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the elapsed duration of lip swelling reduces the ability to trend symptom progression and correlate timing with exposure, but it does not typically change immediate anaphylaxis management when respiratory symptoms are present. This is mainly a documentation precision issue.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures ~30 min post-ingestion onset and left corner location, but does not state it was localized to the upper lip as in the Gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document the exact anatomic location (upper lip) is unlikely to change acute treatment because any progressive orofacial swelling with respiratory complaints warrants urgent anaphylaxis evaluation. It could slightly reduce clarity for monitoring spread/angioedema pattern.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies throat closing sensation; generated lists breathing difficulty and dysphagia but does not explicitly document throat closing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not explicitly documenting a “throat closing” sensation can understate airway involvement, which is a key red-flag feature in suspected anaphylaxis and may influence downstream urgency/triage and risk stratification. Even with breathing difficulty noted, loss of this specific symptom can meaningfully distort severity assessment.

Dizziness can be a marker of systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension) in anaphylaxis; omitting it may reduce recognition of severity and appropriate escalation/monitoring needs. While not always management-changing, it can affect assessment of anaphylaxis progression.

safety_verdicts.content: ~22 y/o F presenting with progressive lip swelling and respiratory difficulty after eating prawn soup (first-time ingestion) at ~19:00
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: While prawn soup trigger and ~19:00 timing are supported by transcript, the composite statement adds unsupported details (“~22 y/o” and “first-time ingestion”). Age cannot be confirmed without visit date, and first-time ingestion is not explicitly stated.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating an approximate age without a visit date and adding “first-time ingestion” introduces inaccuracies that could mislead allergy history interpretation and future counseling. However, the core high-risk clinical picture (food-triggered swelling with respiratory difficulty) remains, so acute safety impact is limited.

safety_verdicts.content: Antihistamine administered at home by mother as interim measure while awaiting ambulance
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript shows the clinician advised taking an antihistamine and asked if any were available; it is not confirmed that an antihistamine was actually administered.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting that an antihistamine was administered when it was only advised can mislead clinicians into thinking symptomatic treatment has already been given and may affect interpretation of response or ongoing symptom progression. In an anaphylaxis scenario, inaccurate medication administration history can impair urgent decision-making and monitoring.
